Customers & loyalty

Customer Loyalty Ladder
Download PDF guide

Interactive loyalty-model prototype

Design for customer value before, during and after the first purchase.

A loyalty ladder helps teams plan the customer relationship from initial interest through first purchase, repeat use, support and voluntary advocacy. Use it to identify friction, create genuinely helpful engagement and improve lifetime value through sustained customer value—not pressure or manipulation.

!
Loyalty is earned, not engineered through dark patterns. Customers do not move in a straight line, and not every satisfied customer wants to advocate publicly. Make communications relevant, consent-based and easy to control; treat re-engagement as an invitation to restore value rather than a reason to create urgency, guilt or friction around leaving.

Plan a customer stage

Choose a stage, define the customer outcome, then plan a helpful activity, a fair measure and a boundary. The strongest loyalty work improves the underlying experience, not merely the volume of messages sent.

Customer loyalty journey

Select a rung to inspect the intended customer outcome, activity, measure and experience boundary.

5/5 Stages mapped
Potential relationship First value exchange Repeat relationship Voluntary support Voluntary advocacy
↺ Loyalty is not linear. Customers can reduce usage, pause or lapse after any stage. Use insight to remove friction and invite re-engagement where appropriate; respect choices to disengage and do not equate silence with consent.

RACE customer lifecycle connection

RACE connects the loyalty ladder to a broader marketing lifecycle: build awareness, prompt useful interaction, enable conversion and sustain customer value through engagement.

Reach

Build relevant awareness and make the offer discoverable for potential prospects.

Act

Enable meaningful interactions such as content use, enquiries, trials or product exploration.

Convert

Make a first purchase, commitment or next step clear, accessible and proportionate.

Engage

Support successful use, retention, repeat value and voluntary advocacy over time.

Lifecycle coverage

Map every stage, then identify the most important friction point rather than trying to optimise all activity at once.

Customer value

The goal is to increase customer value and trust; a larger message volume is not itself evidence of loyalty.

Re-engagement

Lapsed customers may return when a renewed offer addresses a real need, restores trust or removes prior friction.

Using a loyalty ladder well

    This planner supports customer-experience and marketing discussions; it does not replace customer research, consent management, accessibility work or legal review. Handle behavioural and personal data lawfully, minimise collection, protect customer choice and avoid tactics that manufacture dependency, obstruct cancellation or exploit vulnerability.
